exceptional: Unusually good or standing out from the ordinary.
exclusive: Restricted to a particular person or group.
extensive: Covering a wide range or large amount.
feasible: Capable of being done or achieved.
fragile: Weak and easily broken or damaged.
gradual: Taking place slowly in small stages.
heterogeneous: Made up of parts that are different in kind.
homogeneous: Made up of parts that are all the same kind.
identical: Exactly the same in every detail.
immense: Extremely large in size or degree.
inclusive: Including or covering many people or things.
incoherent: Lacking logical connection and hard to understand.
indispensable: Absolutely necessary and impossible to do without.
inevitable: Certain to happen and impossible to avoid.
inherent: Existing in something as a natural and permanent quality.
intangible: Having no physical form and unable to be touched.
integral: Necessary and essential as part of a whole.
interdependent: Mutually dependent and influencing one another.
intermittent: Occurring at irregular intervals; not continuous.
intricate: Very complicated, with many detailed parts.
invalid: Not valid because it lacks a sound basis.
irrelevant: Not connected with or related to the matter at hand.
isolated: Set apart from others; occurring singly.
marginal: Very small in degree or at the edge of importance.
maximal: As great or large as possible.
minimal: As small or as little as possible.
minute: Extremely small and noticeable only on close inspection.
moderate: Average in amount or degree; not extreme.
modest: Not large in size or amount.
mutual: Felt or done by two or more parties toward one another.
negligent: Failing to take proper care over something.
negligible: So small as to be not worth considering.
obsolete: No longer in use because it has become outdated.
opaque: Hard to understand because the meaning is unclear.
overt: Done or shown openly and not concealed.
peculiar: Distinctive and belonging only to a particular thing.
pertinent: Directly relevant to the matter being considered.
plausible: Seeming reasonable and likely to be true.
preceding: Coming before in order or time.
preliminary: Coming before and preparing for the main event.
prevailing: Most common or dominant at a particular time.
prevalent: Widespread and common in a particular place or time.
primitive: Belonging to an early, undeveloped stage.
prior: Coming before in time or order.
profound: Very deep and far-reaching in effect.
prominent: Standing out and important; widely known.
reciprocal: Given or done in return by both sides.
redundant: Not needed because it duplicates something else.
relevant: Directly connected to the matter at hand.
remarkable: Worthy of notice; striking and memorable.
robust: Strong, sturdy, and not easily shaken.
rudimentary: Basic and at the most undeveloped stage.
scarce: Insufficient in quantity relative to demand; rare.
selective: Choosing carefully and accepting only some things.
sparse: Thinly scattered and small in amount.
spontaneous: Happening of itself without external prompting.
sporadic: Occurring at irregular and infrequent intervals.
subordinate: Lower in rank and dependent on something higher.
substantial: Large in amount or degree and real in effect.
subtle: So delicate or precise as to be hard to notice.
successive: Following one after another in sequence.
tangible: Real and able to be perceived or touched.
temporary: Lasting for only a limited time.
transient: Lasting only a short time and quickly passing.
typical: Showing the characteristic qualities of its kind.
ubiquitous: Present everywhere at the same time.
uniform: The same throughout; even and unvarying.
unique: Being the only one of its kind.
valid: Well founded and acceptable on sound grounds.
vast: Very great in size, amount, or extent.
viable: Capable of working successfully or surviving.
vital: Absolutely essential to survival or success.
volatile: Liable to change rapidly or unpredictably; easily evaporated.
widespread: Spread over a wide area or among many people.
accumulate: To gather or build up gradually in quantity.
acquire: To gain knowledge or ability through effort.
advocate: To publicly support a cause; a person who supports a cause.
alter: To change the nature or state of something.
anticipate: To expect something and prepare for it in advance.
approach: A way of dealing with a problem; to come near.
aspect: A particular part or feature of something.
associate: To connect or link two things in one's mind.
assumption: Something accepted as true without proof.
augment: To make something larger by adding to it.
capacity: The maximum amount something can hold or do.
challenge: To question the correctness of something; a difficult task.
characterize: To describe the distinctive qualities of something.
circumstance: A condition or fact that surrounds and affects an event.
clarify: To make something clearer or easier to understand.
coincide: To occur at the same time or to correspond exactly.
component: One of the parts that make up a whole.
comprehend: To understand the meaning of something fully.
comprise: To be made up of several parts.
concept: A general, abstract idea about something.
concern: To relate to or affect something; a matter of interest.
conclude: To reach a decision by reasoning from evidence.
condition: A requirement or state of affairs necessary for something.
confirm: To establish the truth or certainty of something.
consist: To be made up of certain parts.
constituent: A component part of a whole.
constitute: To be the parts that form a whole.
constraint: A limitation that restricts free action.
context: The circumstances and background surrounding an event.
contradict: To assert the opposite of or be inconsistent with something.
contribute: To help bring about a result or to give toward a purpose.
correspond: To match or be in agreement with something.
decline: To decrease gradually in number or strength.
denote: To indicate or refer to a particular meaning.
differentiation: The act of distinguishing or becoming distinct.
dimension: An aspect or measurable extent of something.
diminish: To become or make smaller in size or degree.
display: To show or make something visible.
dispute: To question the correctness of something; an argument.
distribute: To divide and share something among several places or people.
distribution: The way something is spread out or shared.
domain: The range or field that an activity or knowledge covers.
duration: The length of time something continues.
emerge: To come into view or to arise.
emphasize: To give special importance to something.
enhance: To improve the quality or value of something.
establish: To set up something firmly on a solid foundation.
evidence: Facts or information that support a claim.
examination: A careful inspection or investigation of something.
exceed: To go beyond a limit or standard.
exemplify: To serve as a typical example of something.
exhibit: To show or display a quality or feature.
expand: To increase in size, range, or scope.
extend: To make something longer or larger in range or time.
facilitate: To make a process easier or smoother.
function: The particular role or action that something performs.
generate: To produce or bring something into existence.
highlight: To draw attention to something important.
identify: To recognize and determine what something is.
impact: A strong effect that one thing has on another.
incorporate: To include something as part of a whole.
instance: A particular case or example of something.
integrate: To combine parts into a unified whole.
interaction: The act of two or more things affecting each other.
investigation: A careful examination to discover the facts.
involve: To include or necessarily require something.
maintain: To keep something in a continued state, or to assert.
mechanism: The structure or process by which something operates.
obstacle: Something that blocks or hinders progress.
outline: To describe the main points briefly; a summary of structure.
principle: A fundamental law underlying a phenomenon or behavior.
process: A series of steps making up the course of something; to handle.
property: An inherent characteristic that a thing possesses.
quantity: An amount that can be measured or counted.
ratio: The relative relationship between two quantities.
reflect: To show or reveal something, or to throw back light.
resemble: To be similar to something in appearance or quality.
resource: A supply of materials or means that can be used.
reveal: To make something hidden known or visible.
sequence: An ordered arrangement of things following one another.
stability: The state of being steady and not easily changed.
structure: The arrangement of parts that form a whole.
sustain: To keep something going or to support it continuously.
theory: A system of principles organized to explain a phenomenon.
transformation: A major change in form or nature.
transition: A passage from one state or stage to another.
undergo: To experience a change or process directly.
vary: To differ or change in degree or kind.
yield: To produce a result or amount; the amount produced.
